# AI Battery

> AI Battery is a free, open-source macOS menu bar app that shows rate limits, context health and token usage for Claude Code and OpenAI Codex — up to 3 accounts per provider. It reads local session logs for token counts and makes minimal requests to your provider for rate limits. No analytics, no telemetry.

This file is the machine-readable index of **this repository**. The website's equivalent,
covering the product rather than the source, is <https://aibattery.dev/llms.txt>.

## Key facts

- **What it is**: a macOS menu bar app (not a CLI, not a library) for Claude Code and Codex CLI users
- **Platform**: macOS 13 (Ventura) or later, Apple Silicon only — the release binary is arm64-only
- **Language**: Swift 6 / SwiftUI, built with SwiftPM
- **Current version**: 3.4.0, released 2026-11-03 — <https://github.com/KyleNesium/AIBattery/releases/tag/v3.4.0>
- **License**: MIT
- **Dependencies**: Sparkle 2 (auto-update) and Apple frameworks only
- **Tests**: 1743 tests across 132 test files (Swift Testing)
- **Agent access**: an MCP server lets Claude Code read this data in-conversation —
  <https://github.com/KyleNesium/AIBattery-MCP> (Claude accounts only, not Codex)
- **Website**: <https://aibattery.dev>
- **Install**: `brew tap KyleNesium/tap && brew install --cask aibattery`
- **Privacy**: reads Claude Code and Codex CLI JSONL session logs for token counts and context
  health, never message content. No analytics, no telemetry. OAuth refresh tokens live in the
  macOS Keychain; access tokens are memory-only.

## Specs — the source of truth

Code follows `spec/`, not the other way round. Change the spec first, then the code.

- [spec/ARCHITECTURE.md](spec/ARCHITECTURE.md): app structure, data flow, project tree, build config
- [spec/DATA_LAYER.md](spec/DATA_LAYER.md): models, services, algorithms, the ViewModel
- [spec/UI_SPEC.md](spec/UI_SPEC.md): views, layout, colours, typography
- [spec/CONSTANTS.md](spec/CONSTANTS.md): every hardcoded value — thresholds, URLs, timings

## Build and test

```bash
swift build -c release          # build
./scripts/build-app.sh          # the signed .app bundle CI ships (never hand-assemble one)
swift test --no-parallel        # --no-parallel is required; a bare `swift test` deadlocks
```

Three SwiftPM targets: `AIBatteryCore` (all logic, path `AIBattery/`), `AIBattery`
(the `@main` entry point, path `AIBatteryApp/`), `AIBatteryCoreTests`.

## Installing the app with an agent

Do not build from source to install. Use the runbook, which has a check per step and names
what only a person can do (the macOS launch prompt and the provider sign-in):

- [Install runbook](https://aibattery.dev/install.md) (HTML: <https://aibattery.dev/install>)
- [install.sh](https://aibattery.dev/install.sh): pinned to the current release and SHA-256 verified
- [app.json](https://aibattery.dev/app.json): version, download URLs, byte sizes, SHA-256
  checksums, install commands and the guide index, as JSON

## Using AI Battery from an agent

The app is a menu bar UI with no CLI. To let an agent read the same data inside a
conversation, use the companion MCP server:

- [AIBattery-MCP](https://github.com/KyleNesium/AIBattery-MCP): a Model Context Protocol
  server over stdio, with six read-only tools — `get_dashboard`, `get_rate_limits`,
  `get_token_usage`, `get_health`, `get_status`, `get_stats`. It reads this app's stored
  credentials, so the app has to be installed and signed in.
  Its own index: <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/KyleNesium/AIBattery-MCP/main/llms.txt>
- Scope: **Claude accounts only.** It has no Codex tools, even though this app supports Codex.
